title: Two-story house remodel with an east addition and a new basement
source: Schematic design floor plans, elevations and sections (1/4 inch = 1 foot).

gableRoof.note: The existing north-south gable at 4:12, the new east-west gable over the addition at 9:12 with its ridge at the printed building height, and a cross gable over the west bedroom.

stages.label: House
stages.line: A two-story house with a new two-story addition to the east, a new basement under the existing house, a west deck and a covered entry porch. Choose Explore to turn the model or go to a room.

stages.label: Entry side
stages.line: The east side: the new gable end of the addition, its covered porch with steps down to grade, and the front door into the entry.

stages.label: Roofs
stages.line: The roofs lift away: the existing low gable running north to south, a cross gable over the west bedroom, and the steeper new gable over the addition, running east to west.

stages.label: Second floor
stages.line: The second floor: a primary bedroom across the west end with its own bath, a guest bedroom and a second bath in the existing house, and two new bedrooms with closets in the addition.

stages.label: First floor
stages.line: The first floor: dining and kitchen in the existing house, a lounge at the stair, a study and a bath, and the new living room and entry in the addition, with the deck to the west and the porch to the east.

stages.label: Basement
stages.line: The new basement under the existing house, reached by its own stair and by an outside areaway, with gear storage under the deck. The existing basement to the east stays as it is, and the addition sits over a crawl space.

sheetLabel: Static plan of the first floor of a two-story house with an east addition.
assumptions: Levels are printed on the sections: average grade 4 feet 5 inches below the first floor, the second floor 9 feet 7 1/2 inches above it, the top of plate 7 feet above the second floor, the new basement 10 feet 3 inches below the first floor, and the building height 31 feet 2 1/2 inches.

The new roof over the addition is a printed 9:12 gable with its ridge at the building height. The existing roof pitch (about 4:12) and the cross gable over the west bedroom are scaled from the elevations.
The existing basement floor height is scaled from the section; that basement is outside the scope and drawn as an empty room.
The crawl space ground under the addition is assumed 2 feet below grade.
Window sizes and sills come from the elevations; the bath window sills and a few heads not printed are scaled.
The ground is drawn level at the average grade; the plans do not show the slope of the lot.
The deck, its stair and the areaway steps are drawn with equal risers; guards and posts are simplified.
The detached garage and the existing outside stair on the south side are not part of this work and are not drawn.
The roof plan notes that the salvaged solar panels are reinstalled; their layout is not drawn, so they are not shown.
Furniture and fixtures follow the plan symbols where drawn; room areas are not printed, so labels show names only.
